title: Coins for Bombs: The Predictive Ability of On-Chain Transfers for Terrorist Attacks

scopes.description: Complete author-documented Bitcoin data collection, event construction, daily aggregation, event-study bootstrap and machine-learning workflow, including the separate supplied XRP transfer-plot branch.

Separate supplied XRP transfer plotting branch only: read the packaged Figure 3 workbook and produce its long and short date-window plots; this does not reproduce the Bitcoin panel, event study, or machine-learning results.

requirements.description: WalletExplorer wallet and address classifications used to seed X.RData and later address-level collection for the author's study window.

routes.description: The author scrapes WalletExplorer pages. The official API documents address and wallet lookups, but source labels are not updated after 2016 except rare cases; the named-wallet coverage and mapping to the author's study list are not verified.

requirements.description: Per-wallet transaction CSVs consumed by run_Raw with wallet, date, received_amount, sent_amount, sent_to, balance, transaction and received_from fields. Expected fields: wallet; date; received_amount; sent_amount; sent_to; balance; transaction; received_from. Expected coverage period: Transaction dates used in the full sample; exact start and end dates for this input are not specified in run_Raw.

routes.description: The official API documents wallet and address transaction methods, but does not establish the author's CSV field mapping, transaction coverage or a compatible prepared-file export. Supplied scraper outputs are distinct RData schemas and do not establish this CSV contract.

requirements.description: A labels.csv crosswalk with ID and TYPE columns used to classify each wallet before producing type-specific daily exports. Expected fields: ID; TYPE.

routes.description: The supplied workbook is readable, but its first-sheet headings are category headings rather than ID and TYPE; the required crosswalk conversion and category mapping are not documented.

requirements.description: A daily BTC price object named BTC with Date and Close fields, used to value the raw transaction rows in USD; no producer or price source is supplied. Expected fields: Date; Close. Expected coverage period: Every wallet transaction date being processed; source coverage and price units are unspecified.

Wikipedia event rows used to match notable events to GTD, with downstream Date, Country, Location and Year fields; manual cleaning and adjustments are described but no prepared table is included. Expected fields: Date; Country; Location; Year. Expected coverage period: 2015 to 2019-04-30 in the event workflow, with exact cleaned-page coverage unresolved.

routes.description: The supplied scraper parses linked incident tables into Day and other columns, while its cleaner reads Date and later matching uses Country; current page structure and the required author-cleaned contract are not verified.

requirements.description: The GTD event-level workbook used for the 2015 through 2019-04-30 match and event filters. Expected fields: iyear; imonth; iday; country; country_txt; natlty1_txt; attacktype1_txt; weaptype1_txt; nkill; propextent_txt; ransompaid. Expected coverage period: 2015 through the day before 2019-05-01.

routes.description: START lists a full 1970-2020 XLSX product, which covers the author's selected dates; the codebook documents the variables read by the source. Access requires the official brief form and acceptance of terms. The author's specific 0221dist snapshot is absent, so version-specific fidelity remains to be checked after authorized acquisition.

requirements.description: Five separate wide daily group CSVs: EXCHANGE.csv, MIXER.csv, DARKMARKET.csv, SERVICE.csv and GAMBLING.csv; their date, wallet-column and row contracts are unspecified.

The AGG daily panel consumed by run_Boot for event records and the eventstudy call; the source separately creates ALL from the five group tables but never defines AGG or shows that ALL is its equivalent.

The prepared USER.csv read by run_ML, including TYPE, DATE, VOLUME, SIGMA1 and the consumed columns 4:20; full feature names, meanings, joins and a compatible producer are not supplied. Expected fields: TYPE; DATE; VOLUME; SIGMA1; columns 4:20 (remaining predictor definitions unspecified).

The packaged author-prepared XRP daily transfer workbook used by the separate plotting script. Expected fields: Date; Out; In; Total. Expected coverage period: Long plot: 2019-03-29 through 2019-06-30; short plot: 2019-03-29 through 2019-05-30.

routes.description: The exact workbook read by the supplied plot code is present and its bounded first-sheet header probe matches Date, Out, In and Total. The one-row probe does not verify the full date span; the README identifies the attached workbook as underlying data for the XRP plot.
routes.expected_period: Long plot: 2019-03-29 through 2019-06-30; short plot: 2019-03-29 through 2019-05-30.

issues.description: Supplied wallet acquisition paths produce WalletExplorer X.RData, per-wallet AdditionalAddresses, onchain USER.RData, or parse_Wallet DF.RData with different schemas. No supplied stage exports the run_Raw transaction CSV with its complete field contract; the labels workbook does not establish labels.csv; and the source does not identify producers or schemas for the five run_Boot wide group CSVs, AGG, or run_ML USER.csv. Preserve each handoff and do not substitute X, USER, DF or the constructed ALL object for another schema without author evidence.

The remaining event contracts are unresolved after the supported directory and save-name preparation. The collector's Year/Day output versus the cleaner's raw WIKI$Date input and the CSV writer/read paths across working-directory changes have not been confirmed against the author's cleaned input. The supplied cleaner does derive Country from Location and applies the documented aliases/manual corrections. Event state also depends on execution order: get_Notable_Events.R creates a top-level DATES vector from filtered GTD$Date; run_ML consumes global DATES without resetting the environment, so a same-session handoff is possible. run_Boot instead reloads GTD_Notables.RData, reads the GTD$DATES member, and sorts/prunes that vector inside its loop. Whether the saved GTD object contains that member, the intended cohort/order, and whether WIKI_Notables.RData is a separate supplied input remain unknown. The proposed GDT-to-GTD save-name edit addresses only that supported identifier mismatch. These facts do not establish a separate unconditional execution failure after preparation, so the issue records unresolved closure rather than a confirmed blocker.

run_ML states the original per-user loops were omitted, reads USER.csv with no compatible full feature producer, and uses columns 4:20 as predictors. The retained next() calls depend on the omitted loop context and the active bare SVM token has no supported intended replacement. Do not invent predictor names, joins, folds, loop bodies or model code.

The full workflow mixes placeholder local address paths, changed working directories, and absolute Windows paths in raw/ML scripts. The required data root and per-stage output locations are not provided, so a consistent cross-script directory mapping cannot yet be specified.

An active RSelenium/Firefox branch follows a '#not run' comment and calls remDr$close(), launches Firefox, clicks page controls, and issues Windows taskkill for Java. RSelenium is absent locally, and the Windows cleanup command does not match the Linux environment; this branch must remain statically reviewed until its intended role and compatible session cleanup are confirmed.

WalletExplorer's official information page says its name database has not been updated since 2016 except for rare cases; compatible 2015-2019 named-wallet attribution and the author's label list are therefore unverified.

The XRP plot starts by changing to an absolute Windows Figures directory even though its workbook is packaged at Figures/Figure 3 Data.xlsx. A package-root launch supports a local relative path repair.

run_Boot

run_ML

- exports ML results for random forest, SVM, and neural networks

(IV) Attached also the figures and the underlying data for the network analysis plot and Sri Lanka Easter bombing XRP plot.

dependency_review.description: WIKI_NOTABLE_ATTACKS.csv is generated by get_Notable_Events.R before a later read of the same basename; the changed working directory leaves the writer/reader location unresolved under I_EVENTS. This is a generated intermediate, not a separate external input.
The named GTD workbook is a required public input for the event builder; START documents a compatible period and XLSX product with form-based access.
The named GTD_Notables.RData output is attempted with object GDT, while downstream code expects GTD; preserve this as the event producer contract issue.
WIKI_Notables.RData is loaded by the supplied event code, but no save producer for that object file is present in the supplied source.
run_Boot requires all five named wide group CSVs. The per-wallet exports from run_Raw do not establish their expected daily wide schema or producer.
run_Boot and run_ML load GTD_Notables.RData; the supplied event source has the GDT/GTD save mismatch and creates DATES in memory without saving a consumer-ready object.

run_Raw requires labels.csv with ID and TYPE columns; the supplied workbook is not shown to be that crosswalk.

actions.description: Confirm the author wallet-name snapshot and its identity coverage across the 2015-2019 study window. WalletExplorer's current official documentation reports that its name database has been largely unchanged since 2016, so its public API is a candidate discovery route rather than a verified substitute for the author's labels.
steps: Obtain the author-documented wallet cohort or label-source snapshot and record its date coverage and category definitions.

If using the public WalletExplorer route, confirm the required historical name coverage and the exact page/API fields before using it as an input; do not assume newer source labels replicate the author's list.
Keep any address-to-wallet mapping in the working data area and omit address and label records from the assessment output.
validation: After authorized input preparation, compare the mapped wallet set and study-date coverage with the author specification without publishing underlying address or label records.

actions.description: Obtain the author's prepared per-wallet transaction CSV contract or a documented producer that creates it. The supplied onchain USER RData and parse_Wallet DF RData have different fields and do not establish the run_Raw CSV input.
steps: Request the prepared CSV schema, its documented producer and date/amount units for wallet, date, received_amount, sent_amount, sent_to, balance, transaction and received_from.
Keep get_Onchain_Transfers USER RData and parse_Wallet DF RData as distinct outputs; do not deserialize either file or invent a conversion to the required CSV.
Use an author-confirmed prepared CSV route as the primary source if it supplies the required contract; retain raw page/API collection as conditional context.
validation: After authorized input preparation, inspect only the CSV header, column types and documented date range before running run_Raw; compare the generated summary to the source specification without reconstructing the study independently.

actions.description: Request the documented conversion from the packaged category workbook to the labels.csv ID/TYPE crosswalk. The bounded workbook probe does not establish how category columns map to wallet identities or TYPE values.
steps: Obtain the author crosswalk schema, category mapping and intended conversion steps for labels.xlsx to labels.csv.
Convert the workbook only after the ID and TYPE mapping is supported; keep all wallet identifiers and label records out of audit outputs.
validation: After authorized conversion, confirm labels.csv has ID and TYPE columns and that its source category mapping matches the author's description without exposing row values.

actions.description: Request the source and producer for the BTC object consumed by run_Raw, including date coverage and quote units.
steps: Obtain the author's daily price input or documented producer for BTC$Date and BTC$Close, with units, date format and coverage for processed transaction dates.
Preserve the source's 3600 fallback for unmatched dates unless the author specifies an exact alternative.
validation: After authorized input preparation, verify Date/Close coverage and price units against the author's source documentation; do not replace the fallback based on guesswork.

actions.description: Acquire the GTD workbook through START's documented 1970-2020 XLSX route after authorized form access, then compare its release and required columns with the author's named 0221dist file.
steps: Use the official START download form and accept its terms through the authorized data-acquisition process; no form was submitted and no workbook payload was requested in this assessment.
Save the authorized workbook in the configured event-data directory under the filename expected by get_Notable_Events.R, or document the exact supported path configuration.

Compare the acquired release with the author's 0221dist snapshot and confirm the required date, country, nationality, attack-type and weapon-type fields for 2015 through 2019-04-30; do not redistribute raw GTD data.
validation: After authorized acquisition, use a bounded workbook header/date-range check and record the exact release and fields before event construction.

actions.description: Resolve the raw Wikipedia input, directory, and event-state contracts while preserving the supplied Country-from-Location cleanup and explicit overrides. The Year/Day versus WIKI$Date input, CSV path, WIKI_Notables route, and global DATES versus GTD$DATES state sequence remain unverified.
steps: Preserve the supplied Country-from-Location parsing, alias normalization, and manual overrides. Confirm the author's raw WIKI_NOTABLE_ATTACKS.csv headers/date representation and whether the collector's Year/Day output supplies the cleaner's WIKI$Date input; do not invent a conversion or replacement country mapping.

Choose one event working directory and document the matching WIKI_NOTABLE_ATTACKS.csv write/read paths across the collector and cleaner; do not assume equal basenames in different directories identify the same file.

Keep the date vectors distinct: get_Notable_Events.R creates global DATES from filtered GTD$Date, and run_ML consumes that global without resetting the environment, so ordered execution in one R session may provide a handoff. run_Boot reloads GTD_Notables.RData and constructs/sorts/prunes a separate DATES vector from GTD$DATES. Confirm that member's producer and the intended event cohort/order, and whether WIKI_Notables.RData is a separately supplied input; do not invent saves, renames, or filters. The supported GDT-to-GTD edit changes only the saved object identifier.
validation: Before a later authorized run, confirm the raw CSV field/date format and writer/read directories; then statically reconcile the event producer's global DATES with run_ML's same-session use and separately identify the GTD$DATES member consumed after run_Boot reload. Confirm the WIKI_Notables.RData route and preserve the authored event filters/cohort.

actions.description: Correct the supported save-object name mismatch so the event producer saves GTD for the later GTD_Notables.RData load; this does not establish the separate GTD$DATES member or resolve the Wikipedia input and state contracts.

steps: Apply the one-line change in a working copy only after the unresolved event-table and working-directory contracts are documented.
validation: Statically confirm the saved object name matches the later GTD_Notables.RData load. Separately establish whether the saved GTD contains the GTD$DATES member read by run_Boot; this one-line edit does not create that member.

actions.description: Ordered, conditional full workflow for the supplied programs. It retains each authored branch and names the producer-consumer chains while leaving the unsupported schemas and event handoffs explicit.
steps: 1. Configure one working-copy root and stage directories only after the author data paths are known; resolve all current local-address placeholders and absolute paths consistently.

2. Run get_Wallets_Ownership.R as the wallet-page acquisition stage: its source writes links.csv and wallet-specific X RData files. The WalletExplorer request/data route and 2015-2019 name coverage remain unverified.

3. Keep the X-based collection branches separate: get_Bitcoin_Data.R reads X RData and saves USER/AdditionalAddresses RData; get_Onchain_Transfers.R also reads X and saves a different USER RData with Date, Value and Balance. parse_Wallet.R separately loads RData containing l and saves DF RData; its matching l producer and compatibility with the other outputs are unresolved.

4. Run_Raw.R can proceed only after the author-compatible per-wallet transaction CSV, labels.csv and BTC object are prepared. It emits type-specific daily exports and SUMMARY_USD.csv; the supplied scrapers do not establish the required transaction CSV or five downstream wide table formats.

5. Prepare the event stage in order: align WIKI_NOTABLE_ATTACKS.csv writer/reader directories and confirm that the collector's Year/Day output is compatible with the cleaner's WIKI$Date input. Retain the supplied Country-from-Location cleanup, aliases, and manual corrections. In a working copy, use the supported GDT-to-GTD save-name edit. Keep later event state separate: get_Notable_Events.R creates global DATES from filtered GTD$Date, which run_ML can consume in the same R session; run_Boot reloads GTD_Notables.RData and reads/sorts/prunes GTD$DATES. Confirm the GTD$DATES member and intended cohort/order, and whether WIKI_Notables.RData is supplied, before continuing; do not invent saves, member renames, or filters.

6. Run_Boot.R consumes EXCHANGE.csv, MIXER.csv, DARKMARKET.csv, SERVICE.csv and GAMBLING.csv plus GTD_Notables.RData and AGG; its locally constructed ALL is not established as AGG. Retain seed 12345, 50 bootstrap repetitions and event.window 45.

7. Run_ML.R consumes USER.csv and GTD_Notables.RData. Obtain its complete feature producer and omitted outer-loop/session context before attempting it; retain the SIGMA1 filter, event-neighborhood test subset, chronological 70 percent split, 10-fold CV, seed 10 and 500-tree setting.

8. Keep Figures/plotXRPtransfers.R as the separate companion branch using Figures/Figure 3 Data.xlsx; after its relative-path and R-package preparation, its two authored plot windows can be checked independently.
validation: Before a later authorized full run, verify each input filename, data type, header and period against its named consumer, with raw wallet/label records withheld from reports.

Confirm the event CSV writer/reader path and raw schema, the same-session global DATES handoff to run_ML, the distinct GTD$DATES member consumed by run_Boot, and the WIKI_Notables.RData route before event-study or ML work; confirm group panel/AGG and USER.csv contracts separately.
Do not deserialize RData objects, download any dataset, launch the Selenium/browser branch, or run author code during this assessment.

Keep this companion branch separate from the Bitcoin event-study and ML input chain.
validation: Check the full workbook date span and required headers after authorized preparation, then compare the two resulting plots to the supplied author figure artifacts.

review_notes: Full-pipeline inputs and output schemas remain unresolved for the prepared transaction CSV, labels.csv, BTC price object, five group CSVs, AGG panel and USER.csv feature table; public wallet and Wikipedia routes were not queried for data payloads.

The exact registered frozen-catalog name/path search found no paper-domain Bitcoin, wallet, blockchain, GTD or terrorism dataset; generic unrelated catalog fields do not establish a compatible route or data absence.
The separate analysis-only scope uses the supplied XRP plot script and Figure 3 workbook. Its bounded probe confirms the required header names but does not establish full date coverage.

No author R program was imported, parsed, executed or used to deserialize RData; no dataset payload, API response or form was requested, no browser was launched, and no packages or author source files were changed.
The separate Figure Table 5 workbook is a supplied data artifact without a supplied entry point that consumes it; it remains contextual and does not extend the executable scope.
All source edits are proposed fragments in the structured actions and remain unapplied; final readiness and data-status fields are left for the controller finalizer.
